summary: Federal Communications Commission urges preservation of E-Rate program to support broadband infrastructure in schools and libraries. The comment opposes limiting or sunsetting the E-Rate program, emphasizing its importance for modern education infrastructure and student success.

claims.argument: Reducing E-Rate would cost the district between $300,000 and $500,000 annually, competing with other essential resources
claims.evidence_quote: This would cost our district anywhere between $300,000 and $500,000, depending on the year. We spend nearly 80% of our operating revenue on people who work with our students. We would need to reduce staffing or compensation to offset the lost E-Rate revenue.

claims.argument: The program is essential for modern education infrastructure.
claims.evidence_quote: in modern education. As our nation seeks to prepare students for college, careers, and an increasingly technology-driven economy, now is not the time to undermine the very program and related infrastructure that makes those opportunities possible.

filer_raw: Mark Maus, Superintendent, Smithville R-II School District, MO
